title: UNESCO-ICOMOS Report Finds 'Incomparable' War Damage to Preah Vihear Temple
detail: A joint UNESCO-ICOMOS Advisory Mission, on site March 1-6, 2026, published its report documenting 142 damaged areas from the July 2025 fighting and 420 from the December 2025 fighting at Preah Vihear temple. The mission described the scale of destruction as 'incomparable' with earlier rounds of conflict at the site, said 'no area was spared,' and found the temple under 'serious and specific danger,' citing destroyed architectural elements, mutilated decorative features, shrapnel-scarred walls, destabilized cliffs, and explosive remnants of war scattered across the site. Cambodia's Information Minister Neth Pheaktra said 'Preah Vihear Temple is not only Cambodia's heritage, but also the heritage of humanity,' calling for sustained international cooperation on ceasefire guarantees, UXO clearance and conservation.

media.caption: UNESCO-ICOMOS report documents extensive war damage to Preah Vihear temple

title: Information Minister Urges Safe Return of 6,066 Displaced Cambodian Children
detail: Following a displacement-site visit in Preah Vihear province by Deputy PM Hang Chuon Naron and the World Food Programme's Cambodia country director, Information Minister Neth Pheaktra said 6,066 Cambodian children and more than 9,000 women remain among those unable to return home. WFP is providing breakfast and temporary education support at the site. Pheaktra said humanitarian assistance 'could ease the suffering of displaced children but could not replace their homes, schools or right to return to a normal life,' warning that 'temporary arrangements should not become permanent,' and repeated that territory 'could not lawfully be acquired by force, nor could barbed wire, barriers or newly constructed infrastructure create a new international boundary.'

media.caption: Cambodia's Information Minister calls for the safe return of displaced children after a WFP site visit in Preah Vihear
